Dila ra ba ang tinubdan sa lami?

Ang kadaghanan sa lami sa pagkaon gikan gyud sa baho niini, dili lang sa dila!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubber slippers are flexible and elastic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the flexibility and elasticity of rubber slippers, which is a material property. G6-E-5 requires interpreting PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring Alert Levels and demonstrating actions before, during, and after a volcanic eruption. There is no connection to volcanic activity, safety, or alert levels.

copy.en: Rubber slippers are flexible and elastic, so they can bend with your feet and return to their shape after every step.
copy.tl: Ang rubber slippers ay flexible at elastic, kaya kaya nitong yumuko kasama ng iyong mga paa at bumalik sa dating hugis pagkatapos ng bawat hakbang.
copy.bis: Ang rubber slippers flexible ug elastic, busa mahimo kining moyukbo uban sa imong mga tiil ug mobalik sa iyang porma human sa matag lakang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Size alone doesn't decide floating! A small coin sinks, but a big log floats.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses buoyancy (sinking/floating) based on heaviness relative to displaced water, not the movement of objects. The competency G3-F-2 focuses on factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). While heaviness is mentioned, the card does not address movement, so it only shares vocabulary and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Does size decide if something floats?

Size alone doesn't decide floating! A small coin sinks, but a big log floats. What matters is how heavy the object is compared to the water it displaces.
copy.tl:
Ang laki ba ang nagdedesisyon kung lumulutang ang isang bagay?

Hindi laki lang ang dahilan ng paglutang! Lumulubog ang maliit na barya, pero lumulutang ang malaking troso. Ang mahalaga ay kung gaano kabigat ang bagay kumpara sa tubig na inookupa nito.
copy.bis:
Ang gidak-on ba ang nagdesisyon kung molutaw ang usa ka butang?

Dili lang gidak-on ang hinungdan sa paglutaw! Mulunod ang gamay nga sensilyo, pero molutaw ang dako nga troso. Ang importante kung unsa ka bug-at ang butang kumpara sa tubig nga gipuy-an niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A steel ship is super heavy but floats because it's big and hollow inside, full of air! Its wide shape pushes aside lots of water, keeping it on top.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains buoyancy/floating using shape and heaviness, but G3-F-2 is about factors affecting the movement of objects (e.g., how size, shape, heaviness affect motion). Floating is a static equilibrium condition, not movement, so the card does not directly teach the competency's skill.

copy.en:
How does a heavy steel ship float?

A steel ship is super heavy but floats because it's big and hollow inside, full of air! Its wide shape pushes aside lots of water, keeping it on top.
copy.tl:
Paano lumulutang ang mabigat na barkong asero?

Mabigat ang barkong asero pero lumulutang dahil malaki at guwang ang loob, puno ng hangin! Ang malawak niyang hugis nakakatulak ng maraming tubig, kaya nananatili sa ibabaw.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglutaw sa bug-at nga barkong puthaw?

Bug-at ang barkong puthaw pero molutaw tungod kay dako ug guwang ang sulod, puno sa hangin! Ang lapad niyang porma makatulak ug daghang tubig, mao nga nagpabilin sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The boat gets heavier and heavier until it sinks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a boat sinks when water enters, focusing on buoyancy and weight gain. It does not describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect the movement of objects, which is the core of G3-F-2. The mention of 'heavier' is incidental and not used to explore movement characteristics.

copy.en:
What happens if a boat gets a hole?

Water rushes in and pushes out the air that kept it floating! The boat gets heavier and heavier until it sinks. That's why boats need no holes.
copy.tl:
Anong mangyayari kung may butas ang bangka?

Papasok ang tubig at mawawala ang hangin na nagpapalutang dito! Unti-unti itong bumibigat hanggang lumubog. Kaya dapat walang butas ang bangka.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung adunay buslot ang bangka?

Musulod ang tubig ug mawala ang hangin nga nagpalutaw niini! Mabug-at kini hangtod mulunod. Mao nga importante nga walay buslot ang bangka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Push a floating object down into the water—it pops right back up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a push causing an object to move down and then pop up, but it does not demonstrate changing speed or direction in the sense of making it go faster, turn, slow down, or stop. The focus is on buoyancy/water's upward push, not on the general effects of pushes and pulls on motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Push a floating object down into the water—it pops right back up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves pushing an object in water, but it does not explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes or by people. It explains a single buoyancy effect rather than showing ways to move objects such as pushing, pulling, rolling, or carrying.

copy.en: Push a floating object down into the water—it pops right back up! The water's upward push is stronger than your push pushing it down.
copy.tl: Itulak pababa ang lumulutang na bagay—babalik agad pataas! Mas malakas ang tulak pataas ng tubig kaysa sa tulak mo pababa.
copy.bis: Duota paubos ang naglutaw nga butang—mobalik dayon pataas! Mas kusgan ang tulak pataas sa tubig kaysa sa imong tulak paubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Salty sea water is heavier than fresh water! It pushes up harder, so you and other objects float more easily in the sea.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains buoyancy in salt water, not the movement of objects. The competency focuses on factors affecting movement (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). While 'heaviness' is mentioned, the card does not describe how these factors affect movement; it addresses floating, which is a static condition, not motion. This is only tangentially related to the competency's subject.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to float in the sea than in a pool?

Salty sea water is heavier than fresh water! It pushes up harder, so you and other objects float more easily in the sea.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling lumutang sa dagat kaysa sa pool?

Ang tubig-dagat ay mas mabigat dahil sa asin! Mas malakas ang tulak pataas nito, kaya mas madaling lumutang sa dagat.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas sayon molutaw sa dagat kaysa sa pool?

Ang tubig-dagat mas bug-at tungod sa asin! Mas kusgan ang tulak pataas niini, mao nga mas sayon molutaw sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA installs river level sensors to give early warnings of flash floods
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions flash floods, which are an effect of weather disturbances, but it does not describe any effects of weather disturbances. It only describes a warning system, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA installs river level sensors to give early warnings of flash floods
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PAGASA and flash flood warnings, but it does not describe weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal. River level sensors are not the same as storm warning signals, so the card does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How does PAGASA warn us about flash floods?

PAGASA installs river level sensors to give early warnings of flash floods! This is especially important in areas with steep mountains.
copy.tl:
Paano tayo binabalaan ng PAGASA tungkol sa flash floods?

Nag-iinstall ang PAGASA ng river level sensors para sa early warnings ng flash floods! Napakahalaga nito lalo na sa mga lugar na may matatarik na bundok.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbabala sa PAGASA kanato bahin sa flash floods?

Nag-install ang PAGASA og river level sensors para sa early warnings sa flash floods! Importante kaayo kini ilabi na sa mga lugar nga adunay dik-as nga bundok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do city streets flood so fast after rain?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains urban flooding due to impervious surfaces, but does not describe effects of a weather disturbance (e.g., typhoon, monsoon) in or near the Philippines. Flooding from rain is only tangentially related to weather disturbances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All the rain becomes runoff, causing street flooding!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rain becoming runoff, which is part of the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It focuses on urban surfaces preventing absorption, not on evaporation, condensation, precipitation, or the cycle's environmental role.

copy.en:
Why do city streets flood so fast after rain?

In cities like Metro Manila, flat concrete and asphalt don't absorb rainwater. All the rain becomes runoff, causing street flooding!
copy.tl:
Bakit mabilis bumaha sa kalye ng siyudad pag-ulan?

Sa mga siyudad tulad ng Metro Manila, ang patag na concrete at asphalt hindi sumisipsip ng ulan. Lahat ng ulan ay nagiging runoff, kaya bumabaha sa kalye!
copy.bis:
Ngano paspas mobaha sa kalye sa siyudad pag-ulan?

Sa mga siyudad sama sa Metro Manila, ang patag nga concrete ug asphalt dili mosupsop sa ulan. Ang tanan nga ulan mahimong runoff, mao nga mobaha sa kalye!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absorbs rainwater to stop urban flooding
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes green infrastructure as a way to absorb rainwater and prevent urban flooding. It does not describe the effects of weather disturbances (e.g., heavy rain, typhoons, storm surges) that occur in or near the Philippines. It addresses a mitigation strategy rather than the disturbances themselves, so it is only related to the competency's topic.

copy.en: Parks, street trees, and permeable pavement act like giant sponges! This green infrastructure absorbs rainwater to stop urban flooding before it becomes runoff.
copy.tl: Ang mga parke, puno sa kalye, at permeable pavement ay parang higanteng espongha! Ang green infrastructure na ito ay sumisipsip ng ulan para pigilan ang urban flooding.
copy.bis: Ang mga parke, puno sa karsada, ug permeable pavement sama sa mga higanteng espongha! Ang green infrastructure nagsipsip sa ulan aron pugngan ang urban flooding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A flood is simply water that covers land which is usually dry!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines what a flood is. It does not describe effects of weather disturbances occurring in or near the Philippines, nor does it connect floods to any specific weather disturbance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A flood is simply water that covers land which is usually dry!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a basic definition of a flood but does not describe how weather changes affect daily activities or explain why certain weather types are dangerous to people.

copy.en: A flood is simply water that covers land which is usually dry!
copy.tl: Ang baha ay tubig na tumatabon sa lupang karaniwang tuyo!
copy.bis: Ang baha mao ang tubig nga motabon sa yuta nga sagad uga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A floodplain is the flat land right beside a river!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a floodplain as a landform beside a river but does not identify local examples or describe how landforms/water bodies influence living and non-living components, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floods very easily whenever the river overflows its banks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains river overflow flooding but does not describe effects of weather disturbances in or near the Philippines, such as typhoons or storms. No connection to weather disturbances is made.

copy.en:
What is a floodplain and why does it flood?

A floodplain is the flat land right beside a river! It floods very easily whenever the river overflows its banks.
copy.tl:
Ano ang floodplain at bakit itong madaling bahain?

Ang floodplain ay ang patag na lupa sa tabi ng ilog! Madali itong bahain kapag umapaw na ang tubig sa ilog.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang floodplain ug ngano nga dali kini mabahaan?

Ang floodplain mao ang patag nga yuta tupad sa suba! Dali kini mabahaan kon moawas na ang tubig sa suba.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pollen from the stamen is tiny, like dust. When lots of it floats in the air, it gets into your nose and can make you sneeze
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Pollen as an allergen is adjacent to pollination; the card does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as reproductive methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it gets into your nose and can make you sneeze — a pollen allergy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Mentions the nose as an entry point, but does not identify nose, windpipe, and lungs or describe how they work.

copy.en:
Why can pollen make you sneeze?

Pollen from the stamen is tiny, like dust. When lots of it floats in the air, it gets into your nose and can make you sneeze — a pollen allergy.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagpapabahing ang pollen?

Ang pollen na ginagawa ng stamen ay napakaliit, parang alikabok. Kapag marami nito sa hangin, nakakapasok ito sa ilong at nagpapabahing — ito ang allergy sa pollen.
copy.bis:
Nganong makapabahing ang pollen?

Ang pollen nga gihimo sa stamen gamay kaayo, murag abog. Kung daghan kini sa hangin, mosulod kini sa ilong ug mopabahing — kini ang pollen allergy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pod of mung beans or string beans that we treat as vegetables is actually a kind of dry fruit, with seeds kept inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Dry pods with seeds are an outcome of seed production; the card does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a kind of dry fruit, with seeds kept inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: A fruit pod with seeds is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en:
Are all fruits juicy?

Not all fruits are juicy — the pod of mung beans or string beans that we treat as vegetables is actually a kind of dry fruit, with seeds kept inside.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng prutas ay matubig?

Hindi lahat ng prutas ay matubig — ang balot ng munggo o sitaw na itinuturing nating gulay ay isang uri ng tuyong prutas, na may mga butong nakatago sa loob.
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga prutas tubigon?

Dili tanan nga prutas tubigon — ang sapot sa monggo o sitaw nga atong giisip nga utanon usa ka klase sa mala nga prutas, nga adunay mga liso sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absorbs ultraviolet light and emits visible light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions UV and visible light but does not compare their wavelengths or frequencies, which is the core skill of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absorbs ultraviolet light and emits visible light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fluorescence but does not explain EMR as energy from vibrating charged particles or as transverse waves, which the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do highlighters glow under UV light?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of UV light causing fluorescence, but it does not identify practical applications of EMR in the sense of telecommunications or medicine; it is more a phenomenon than an application.

copy.en:
Why do highlighters glow under UV light?

It’s called fluorescence! The material absorbs ultraviolet light and emits visible light, making highlighter ink and white clothes glow brightly.
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-glow ang mga highlighter sa ilalim ng UV light?

Fluorescence ang tawag dito! Sumisipsip ang materyal ng ultraviolet light at naglalabas ng visible light, kaya nag-glow ang highlighter at puting damit.
copy.bis:
Ngano nag-glow ang mga highlighter ilalom sa UV light?

Fluorescence ang tawag ani! Nagsipsip ang materyal og ultraviolet light ug nagagawas og visible light, mao nga nag-glow ang highlighter ug puting sinina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there is no evidence at all that he invented the fluorescent lamp
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a famous Filipino (Agapito Flores) but explicitly refutes that he invented the fluorescent lamp. It does not identify any invention by a scientist, so it does not directly support the competency of identifying a scientist and their invention. It is only related to the broader topic of Filipino scientists and inventions.

copy.en: Agapito Flores was a real Filipino electrician! However, there is no evidence at all that he invented the fluorescent lamp.
copy.tl: Si Agapito Flores ay isang totoong Pilipinong elektrisyan! Pero walang ebidensiyang siya ang nag-imbento ng fluorescent lamp.
copy.bis: Si Agapito Flores usa ka tinuod nga Pilipinong elektrisyan! Apan walay ebidensiya nga siya ang nag-imbento sa fluorescent lamp.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A fly has only two wings.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of wings a fly has. It does not describe the role of wings in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en:
How many wings does a fly have?

A fly has only two wings.
copy.tl:
Ilang pakpak ang langaw?

Ang langaw ay may dalawang pakpak lamang.
copy.bis:
Pila ka pako ang langaw?

Ang langaw duha ra ka pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One glide usually covers about 50 meters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a distance value for a glide but does not involve measuring or describing changes in position relative to an original position, nor moving closer/farther/left/right.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One glide usually covers about 50 meters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions distance but provides no time measurement, no simple equipment, and no measuring activity, so it does not directly support measuring distance and time when things move.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How far can a flying fish glide?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses glide distance, not the outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and food gathering; wings are not described.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: by linking several glides together, a flying fish can travel more than 100 meters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavior and distance, not how an animal has changed to better suit its environment through mimicry, camouflage, or similar adaptation.

copy.en:
How far can a flying fish glide?

One glide usually covers about 50 meters, but by linking several glides together, a flying fish can travel more than 100 meters!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayo makalipad ang flying fish?

Karaniwang umaabot ng 50 metro ang isang glide, pero kaya nitong lumipad nang mahigit 100 metro kapag pinagsama-sama ang ilang glide!
copy.bis:
Unsa kalayo ang makalupad sa flying fish?

Kasagaran moabot og 50 metros ang usa ka glide, apan makahimo kini molupad og kapin 100 metros kung sumpayon ang daghang glide!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: she folds her tail skin into a snug little hammock
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a body part (tail skin) but its role is carrying the baby, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency. No support for the specified functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother flying lemur carries her baby clinging to her belly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a parent caring for offspring, which is a form of dependence, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs (air, food, water, shelter). The interaction is parental care, not the dependency described in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother flying lemur carries her baby
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies the flying lemur gives birth to live young (it is a mammal), but it does not identify groups that give birth vs. lay eggs, nor does it contrast mammals with birds/reptiles. The card only shows a mother carrying a baby, not the reproductive mode classification.

copy.en: A mother flying lemur carries her baby clinging to her belly even while gliding through the air — she folds her tail skin into a snug little hammock to keep it safe!
copy.tl: Dala-dala ng inang kagwang ang sanggol nitong nakakapit sa tiyan kahit habang naglilipad-lipad — nino-fold niya ang balat malapit sa buntot para maging parang duyan!
copy.bis: Gidala sa inahang kagwang ang iyang anak nga nagkapyot sa tiyan bisan samtang naglupad-lupad — gipilo niya ang panit duol sa ikog aron mahimong sama sa duyan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The load becomes compressive force pushed downward and outward to the abutments.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a compressive force acting on an arch bridge, which illustrates that forces act between objects, but it does not address the 'can be measured' part of the competency. It is a specific structural example rather than instruction on identifying forces generally or measuring them.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The load becomes compressive force pushed downward and outward to the abutments.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a force situation in an arch bridge, but it does not identify or describe balanced or unbalanced forces, nor does it use the everyday examples named in the competency (box on inclined plane, standing man, constant velocity, falling fruit, accelerating car). The bridge example is not framed in terms of balanced/unbalanced forces.

copy.en:
How does an arch bridge hold up heavy loads without falling?

The load becomes compressive force pushed downward and outward to the abutments. The keystone at the crown holds it all — remove it and the arch collapses!
copy.tl:
Paano kaya kaya ng arch bridge ang mabibigat na karga nang hindi gumuguho?

Ang bigat ay nagiging compressive force na ipinapasa pababa at palabas sa mga abutment. Ang keystone sa gitna ang hawak ng buong arko — tanggalin mo ito at guguhoin ang arko!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdala sa arch bridge sa bug-at nga karga nga dili mahugno?

Ang karga nahimong compressive force nga gipadala paubos ug palabas ngadto sa abutments. Ang keystone sa tuktok ang nagkupot sa tanan — kuhaa ug mahugno ang arko!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An electromagnet is a magnet made using electricity! When current flows through a wire coiled around iron, it becomes a magnet. Turn the current off, and the magnetism stops!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the basic principle of an electromagnet (current through a coil around iron creates magnetism, stopping when current stops) but does not guide the student in making a simple electromagnet or in observing and recording its properties, which is the action required by the competency.

copy.en: An electromagnet is a magnet made using electricity! When current flows through a wire coiled around iron, it becomes a magnet. Turn the current off, and the magnetism stops!
copy.tl: Ang electromagnet ay magnet na gawa gamit ang kuryente! Kapag dumaloy ang current sa wire na nakapulupot sa bakal, nagiging magnet ito. Patayin ang kuryente, mawala ang magnetism!
copy.bis: Ang electromagnet usa ka magnet nga gihimo gamit ang kuryente! Kung moagos ang current sa wire nga giliyok sa puthaw, mahimo kining magnet. Patya ang kuryente, mawala ang magnetism!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's greater on rough surfaces than smooth ones.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the factual relationship between surface roughness and friction magnitude, which is background knowledge for the investigation, but it does not address planning or carrying out a scientific investigation as required by the competency.

copy.en: Friction is a force that opposes motion when two surfaces rub together, making a rolling ball slow and stop! It's greater on rough surfaces than smooth ones.
copy.tl: Ang friction ay isang force na sumasalungat sa galaw kapag nagkikiskisan ang dalawang surface, kaya bumabagal at humihinto ang gumugulong na bola! Mas malaki ito sa magaspang kaysa makinis.
copy.bis: Ang friction usa ka force nga mosupak sa paglihok kung magkuskos ang duha ka surface, mao nga mohinay ug mohunong ang nagligid nga bola! Mas dako kini sa gansang kaysa hamis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rope knot holds tight because of friction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about friction in knots but does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation, nor does it address different surfaces and the size of frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But if the rope is slippery, like when oiled, the knot loosens easily!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a slippery (oiled) rope reduces friction, which touches on reducing friction, but it does not demonstrate friction producing heat or investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction in a systematic way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The rope presses against itself to stop slipping.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how friction affects the movement of a knot, but it does not explore or describe things that affect movement of objects such as size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture in a general sense; it only mentions slipperiness of the rope.

copy.en: A rope knot holds tight because of friction! The rope presses against itself to stop slipping. But if the rope is slippery, like when oiled, the knot loosens easily!
copy.tl: Ang buhol ng lubid ay humahawak dahil sa friction! Nagdidiit ang lubid para hindi madulas. Pero kung madulas ito, tulad ng nilangisan, mas madaling kumalas ang buhol!
copy.bis: Ang buhol sa pisi mokupot tungod sa friction! Nagdikit ang pisi aron dili modanlog. Apan kung danlog kini, sama sa gilanahan, mas sayon mabadbad ang buhol!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spilled oil or water drops the friction between tires and the road!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that oil/water reduces friction but does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces. It provides background knowledge about friction reduction, not the investigation skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spilled oil or water drops the friction between tires and the road!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a way to reduce friction (oil/water) but does not demonstrate how friction produces heat, nor does it investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction in a systematic manner. It only gives a single example of reduced friction, not the full competency.

copy.en:
Why are wet or oily roads dangerous for cars?

Spilled oil or water drops the friction between tires and the road! With less grip, tires can slide or skid when braking, so drivers must be extra careful in the rain.
copy.tl:
Bakit mapanganib ang basang o may langis na kalsada?

Nababawasan ang friction sa pagitan ng gulong at kalsada kapag may natapong langis o tubig! Dahil kulang ang grip, pwedeng dumulas ang gulong, kaya dapat mag-ingat ang mga driver tuwing umuulan.
copy.bis:
Ngano delikado ang basa o nalangisan nga dalan para sa mga sakyanan?

Mokunhod ang friction tali sa ligid ug dalan kung adunay nalangis o nabasa! Tungod sa kulang nga grip, mahimong modanlog ang ligid, mao nga dapat mag-amping ang mga drayber kung mag-ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Friction! As the pencil rubs the paper, tiny bits of graphite scrape off and stick to its rough surface.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a friction phenomenon involving different surfaces (paper vs. glass) but does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of surfaces on frictional force. It provides no investigation steps, variables, or measurement, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Friction! As the pencil rubs the paper, tiny bits of graphite scrape off and stick to its rough surface.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction and surface roughness but does not demonstrate friction producing heat, nor does it investigate ways of reducing or increasing friction. The content is only a simple explanation of why a pencil writes, not a demonstration or investigation of friction's heat production or control.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can't write on super smooth glass!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on surface texture affecting movement (writing on rough paper vs. smooth glass), but it does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect the movement of objects in a general sense. It is a specific example of friction, not a broader exploration of factors affecting movement.

copy.en:
How does a pencil write on paper?

Friction! As the pencil rubs the paper, tiny bits of graphite scrape off and stick to its rough surface. It can't write on super smooth glass!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakasulat ang lapis sa papel?

Dahil sa friction! Habang kinukuskos ng lapis ang papel, natatanggal ang maliliit na graphite at dumidikit sa magaspang na ibabaw nito. Hindi ito makakasulat sa sobrang makinis na salamin!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsulat sa lapis sa papel?

Tungod sa friction! Samtang gikuskos sa lapis ang papel, ang gagmay nga graphite matangtang ug modikit sa gansang nawong niini. Dili kini makasulat sa hamis kaayo nga salamin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Friction! The metal presses tightly against the wood.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why nails/screws stay in wood due to friction, but does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it address the effect of different surfaces on frictional force size.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A screw grips even better because its spiral thread adds extra friction to hold it in place!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction and that a screw's thread adds extra friction, but it does not demonstrate friction producing heat nor investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why don't nails and screws just fall out of wood?

Friction! The metal presses tightly against the wood. A screw grips even better because its spiral thread adds extra friction to hold it in place!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi basta-basta nahuhulog ang pako at turnilyo sa kahoy?

Friction! Mahigpit na nakadikit ang metal sa kahoy. Mas matindi ang hawak ng turnilyo dahil ang spiral thread niya ay nagdadagdag ng friction para manatili!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili basta-basta matagak ang lansang ug turnilyo sa kahoy?

Friction! Hugpit nga nagdikit ang metal sa kahoy. Mas kusog ang kupot sa turnilyo kay ang spiral thread niini nagdugang og friction aron magpabilin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Static friction holds it tightly in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes static versus sliding friction but does not address planning or carrying out an investigation, nor the effect of different surfaces on frictional force.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Once it starts sliding, the friction gets weaker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses friction strength but does not demonstrate friction producing heat or investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Static friction holds it tightly in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies a friction force between the cabinet and floor but does not identify that forces can be measured or address measurement of forces.

copy.en: Pushing a heavy cabinet is hardest at the start! Static friction holds it tightly in place. Once it starts sliding, the friction gets weaker, making it easier to push!
copy.tl: Ang pagtulak ng mabigat na aparador ay pinakamahirap sa simula! Mahigpit itong hawak ng static friction. Pagkadulas na, humihina ang friction, kaya mas madali na itong itulak!
copy.bis: Ang pagtulak sa bug-at nga aparador pinakalisod sa sinugdanan! Hugpit kini gikupot sa static friction. Kung modanlog na, mihina ang friction, mao nga mas sayon na kining itulak!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lens is clear material like glass that bends light to enlarge or focus an image! A mirror, on the other hand, reflects light so we see our reflection.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a simple conceptual statement that lenses bend light and mirrors reflect light, with eyeglasses and mirrors as everyday examples. However, the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card does not support the investigation, illustration, or the specific equipment and mirror types, so it is useful background rather than direct instruction.

copy.en:
How do eyeglasses and mirrors work with light?

A lens is clear material like glass that bends light to enlarge or focus an image! A mirror, on the other hand, reflects light so we see our reflection.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang eyeglasses at mirrors sa liwanag?

Ang lens ay malinaw na materyal tulad ng salamin na nagbabaluktot ng liwanag para palakihin o i-focus ang larawan! Ang mirror naman ay nagbabalik ng liwanag para makita ang repleksyon.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtrabaho sa eyeglasses ug mirrors sa kahayag?

Ang lens usa ka tin-aw nga materyal sama sa salamin nga mobawog sa kahayag aron padakuon o i-focus ang hulagway! Ang mirror mobalik sa kahayag aron makita ang repleksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The six kinds are lever, pulley, inclined plane, wheel and axle, wedge, and screw.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the six simple machines and states their general purpose. It does not provide examples or uses of simple machines found at home, at school, or in the community, which is the specific action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Simple machines make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a general definition of simple machines but does not demonstrate advantages and limitations through guided investigation, nor does it discuss specific machines like inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys in terms of their advantages and limitations.

copy.en: Simple machines make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force! The six kinds are lever, pulley, inclined plane, wheel and axle, wedge, and screw.
copy.tl: Ang simple machines ay nagpapadali ng trabaho sa pamamagitan ng pagbabago ng laki o direksyon ng force! Ang anim na uri ay lever, pulley, inclined plane, wheel and axle, wedge, at screw.
copy.bis: Ang simple machines makapasayon sa trabaho pinaagi sa pag-usab sa gidak-on o direksyon sa force! Ang unom ka klase mao ang lever, pulley, inclined plane, wheel and axle, wedge, ug screw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light scatters off millions of tiny water droplets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes light scattering in fog, not reflection using mirrors or refraction using lenses/prisms as required by G8-F-11. It shares the broad topic of light but does not support the specific investigation of reflection/refraction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you can see a car's light beam
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a light source (car headlight) and its visibility, but does not identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy in the community. It is only tangentially related to light sources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light scatters off millions of tiny water droplets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavior of light (scattering) but does not involve guided activities to explore sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses. It is a factual statement rather than an activity supporting the competency.

copy.en: In thick fog, you can see a car's light beam! This happens because light scatters off millions of tiny water droplets floating in the air.
copy.tl: Sa makapal na hamog, makikita mo ang sinag ng ilaw ng sasakyan! Nangyayari ito dahil ang liwanag ay kumakalat sa milyun-milyong maliliit na patak ng tubig sa hangin.
copy.bis: Sa baga nga gabon, makita nimo ang silaw sa suga sa sakyanan! Mahitabo kini tungod kay ang kahayag mokatag sa minilyon nga gagmay nga tinulo sa tubig nga naglutaw sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's really just a cloud touching the ground — made the same way, of water droplets floating in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes what fog is (a ground-level cloud of water droplets) but does not teach identification of weather characteristics such as temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It only touches on cloud cover indirectly and provides no instructional support for the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made the same way, of water droplets floating in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water droplets in the air, which is a component of the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It provides no explanation of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, or the cycle's environmental significance. Thus it is only related background, not direct support.

copy.en: That thick mist on a mountain or cold morning? It's really just a cloud touching the ground — made the same way, of water droplets floating in the air!
copy.tl: Ang makapal na hamog sa bundok o malamig na umaga? Isa lang talagang ulap na dumikit sa lupa — pareho ang ginagawa nito, patak ng tubig na lumulutang sa hangin!
copy.bis: Ang baga nga gabon sa bukid o bugnaw nga buntag? Usa lang gyud ka panganod nga midikit sa yuta — pareho ra ang pagkahimo niini, tulo sa tubig nga naglutaw sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Sun is the first source of energy in the chain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun as the energy source for food chains but does not involve drawing a food chain, using Philippine living things, or labeling herbivores/carnivores/omnivores as required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Sun is the first source of energy in the chain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the trophic levels of an organism as levels of energy in a food pyramid
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the Sun is the first energy source but does not describe trophic levels as levels of energy in a food pyramid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Sun is the first source of energy in the chain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use examples of food pyramids to describe the transfer of energy between organisms from one trophic level to another
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy transfer from the Sun to plants but does not use food pyramid examples or describe transfer between trophic levels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants use its light to make food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that plants use sunlight to make food, which is a basic prerequisite for understanding photosynthesis, but it does not describe the process, raw materials, or products of photosynthesis or respiration.

copy.en:
Where does almost every food chain start?

With the Sun. Plants use its light to make food, so the Sun is the first source of energy in the chain.
copy.tl:
Saan nagsisimula ang halos lahat ng food chain?

Sa araw. Ginagamit ng mga halaman ang liwanag ng araw para gumawa ng pagkain, kaya ang araw ang unang pinagmulan ng enerhiya.
copy.bis:
Asa nagsugod ang halos tanang food chain?

Sa adlaw. Gamiton sa mga tanom ang kahayag sa adlaw aron makahimo og pagkaon, mao nga ang adlaw mao ang unang tinubdan sa enerhiya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A healthy body needs three kinds of food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes food groups (go, grow, glow) for a balanced diet, not the identification of basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. Food is one basic need, but the card does not teach identifying basic needs; it teaches nutrition categories.

copy.en: A healthy body needs three kinds of food: 'go' foods like rice for energy, 'grow' foods like fish and meat to build the body, and 'glow' foods like fruits and vegetables for protection.
copy.tl: Para lumusog, kailangan ng katawan ang tatlong uri ng pagkain: 'go' na nagbibigay-lakas tulad ng kanin, 'grow' na pampalaki tulad ng isda't karne, at 'glow' na pananggol tulad ng gulay at prutas.
copy.bis: Aron mahimsog, kinahanglan sa lawas ang tulo ka matang sa pagkaon: 'go' nga naghatag kusog sama sa kan-on, 'grow' nga pangpadako sama sa isda ug karne, ug 'glow' nga pangpanalipod sama sa utanon ug prutas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After digestion and absorption, nutrients travel in the blood to every cell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about digestion, absorption, and nutrient transport to body cells. G9-L-9 requires describing biotic and abiotic features of specific ecosystems (rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, coral reefs). No ecosystem content is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After digestion and absorption, nutrients travel in the blood to every cell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how food becomes useful after reaching body cells via blood. G5-L-9 is about animals changing to suit their environment (mimicry, camouflage). No adaptation content is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When is food useful to the body?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food, which is one of the basic needs in G3-L-6, but it does not teach identifying basic needs (air, food, water, shelter). It focuses on the physiological process of nutrient delivery, not the concept of basic needs.

copy.en:
When is food useful to the body?

When it reaches the body cells! After digestion and absorption, nutrients travel in the blood to every cell.
copy.tl:
Kailan nagiging kapaki-pakinabang ang pagkain sa katawan?

Kapag umabot na ito sa mga body cells! Pagkatapos ng digestion at absorption, naglalakbay ang nutrients sa dugo papunta sa bawat cell.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mahimong mapuslanon ang pagkaon sa lawas?

Kon moabot na kini sa mga body cells! Human sa digestion ug absorption, mobiyahe ang mga nutrients sa dugo paingon sa matag cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: bad smell, changed color, mushy spots, or fuzzy mold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes signs of food spoilage (odor, color change, mold) but does not teach these as indicators of a chemical reaction. It lacks the chemical reaction context (precipitate, gas release, temperature change) and does not support the competency's skill of describing chemical reaction indicators.

copy.en: You can tell spoiled food by its bad smell, changed color, mushy spots, or fuzzy mold—it is no longer safe to eat!
copy.tl: Makikilala mo ang bulok na pagkain sa masangsang na amoy, nagbagong kulay, malambot na bahagi, o amag—hindi na ito ligtas kainin!
copy.bis: Mailhan nimo ang dunot nga pagkaon sa baho, nausab nga kolor, humok nga bahin, o agup-op—dili na kini luwas kan-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Storing food cold in a refrigerator slows the microbes down and keeps it fresh longer.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains food spoilage due to microbial multiplication and refrigeration slowing microbes. This is about microbial growth, not the factors affecting rates of chemical reactions (e.g., temperature, concentration) as applied to food preservation. It shares the food preservation context but does not directly teach chemical reaction rate factors.

copy.en:
Why does food spoil, and how can we keep it fresh?

Food spoils because microbes multiply in it! Storing food cold in a refrigerator slows the microbes down and keeps it fresh longer.
copy.tl:
Bakit nabubulok ang pagkain, at paano ito mapapanatiling sariwa?

Nabubulok ang pagkain dahil sa pagdami ng mga mikrobyo! Ang pagtatago sa lamig na refrigerator ay nagpapabagal sa kanila at nagpapatagal sa pagkain.
copy.bis:
Nganong madunot ang pagkaon, ug unsaon pagpreskohon og dugay?

Madunot ang pagkaon tungod kay nagdaghan ang mga mikrobyo! Ang pagtipig sa bugnaw nga refrigerator makapahinay kanila ug makapadugay sa kapresko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Everything in a food web is connected — remove just one species, and others can suddenly become too few or too many
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Food-web connectedness is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: remove just one species, and others can suddenly become too few or too many, throwing off the whole ecosystem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: Species removal throwing off an ecosystem is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: others can suddenly become too few or too many, throwing off the whole ecosystem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: Numbers going up or down is not competition or predation as exemplified in G6-L-6.

copy.en: Everything in a food web is connected — remove just one species, and others can suddenly become too few or too many, throwing off the whole ecosystem.
copy.tl: Magkaugnay ang lahat sa isang food web — kapag nawala ang isang species, maaaring magkulang o sumobra ang iba, na makakaapekto sa buong ecosystem.
copy.bis: Nagkadugtong ang tanan sa usa ka food web — kung mawala ang usa ka species, mahimong makulang o mosobra ang uban, nga makaapekto sa tibuok ecosystem.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A food web shows many food chains linked together in an ecosystem, where one animal can be eaten by more than one kind of predator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Linked food chains is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: A food web shows many food chains linked together in an ecosystem, where one animal can be eaten by more than one kind of predator.
copy.tl: Ang food web ay nagpapakita ng maraming magkaugnay na food chain sa isang ekosistema, kung saan maaaring kainin ng higit sa isang predator ang isang hayop.
copy.bis: Ang food web nagpakita sa daghang magkaugnay nga food chain sa usa ka ekosistema, diin ang usa ka mananap mahimong kaonon sa labaw pa sa usa ka predator.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They stay forever because there is no wind or water on the Moon to wipe or blow them away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon but does not involve observing or describing the Moon as a celestial object; it explains why footprints persist due to lack of wind/water, which is not the skill of observing/describing natural objects in the sky.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They stay forever because there is no wind or water on the Moon to wipe or blow them away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their features, or composition. It only gives a fact about the Moon's environment, which is not directly supporting the competency.

copy.en:
Why do astronaut footprints stay on the Moon for so long?

They stay forever because there is no wind or water on the Moon to wipe or blow them away!
copy.tl:
Bakit nananatili nang napakatagal ang mga bakas ng paa ng mga astronaut sa Buwan?

Nananatili sila nang matagal dahil walang hangin o tubig sa Buwan na pwedeng magpunas o magpalipad sa mga ito!
copy.bis:
Nganong magpabilin og dugay kaayo ang mga tunob sa tiil sa mga astronaut sa Bulan?

Magpabilin sila og dugay kay walay hangin o tubig didto sa Bulan nga makapapas o makapalid niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When two forces are equal and opposite, they cancel out! The object stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the general effect of balanced forces (staying still or constant speed) but does not identify or describe everyday situations such as a box on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an accelerating car. It provides background knowledge rather than directly supporting the competency's skill of identifying and describing everyday examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The object stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the outcome of balanced forces, which is related to inertia, but it does not identify inertia as the tendency to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force. It lacks the concept of inertia and the role of an unbalanced net force, so it only supports background understanding.

copy.en: When two forces are equal and opposite, they cancel out! The object stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed.
copy.tl: Kapag magkapantay at magkasalungat ang dalawang puwersa, nagkakansela sila! Mananatiling nakatayo ang bagay o magpapatuloy sa pare-parehong bilis.
copy.bis: Kung pareho ug balanse pero magkasukwahi ang duha ka puwersa, mag-cancel-out sila! Magpabilin nga nagbarug o magpadayon sa parehas nga tulin.

copy.en:
What happens when you push harder?

The stronger your force, the bigger the change in motion! Push a ball gently and it rolls slowly. Push it hard and it rolls faster and farther. The change depends on how strong your force is!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag mas malakas ang tulak mo?

Mas malakas ang force mo, mas malaki ang pagbabago sa galaw! Bahagyang tulak ang bola, mahina ang gulong; malakas na tulak, mas mabilis at mas malayo. Ang pagbabago ay nakadepende sa lakas ng force!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung mas kusog ang imong duso?

Mas kusog ang imong force, mas dako ang kausaban sa lihok! Hinay nimong iduso ang bola ug hinay kini moligid. Kusog nimong iduso ug mas paspas ug mas layo kini moligid. Ang kausaban nagdepende sa kakusog sa imong force!

A force is a push or a pull that can make an object move, stop, or change its shape!

Ano ba ang pwersa?

Ang pwersa ay isang tulak o hila na maaaring magpagalaw, magpahinto, o magpabago ng hugis ng isang bagay!
copy.bis:
Unsa man ang pwersa?

Ang pwersa usa ka pagtukmod o pagbira nga makapalihok, makapahunong, o makapausab sa porma sa usa ka butang!

copy.en: Fish have smooth, pointed shapes to reduce water friction, letting them swim fast! People copy this shape for boats and ships to move easily.
copy.tl: Ang mga isda ay may makinis at patulis na hugis para bawasan ang water friction, kaya mabilis silang lumangoy! Ginaya ito ng tao sa mga bangka.
copy.bis: Ang mga isda adunay hamis ug talinis nga porma aron pamenusan ang water friction, mao nga paspas silang molangoy! Gisundog kini sa tawo sa mga sakayan.

copy.en: Friction helps us not slip, just like the good grip of shoes on the floor!
copy.tl: Tumutulong ang friction para hindi tayo madulas, gaya ng dikit ng sapatos sa sahig!
copy.bis: Ang friction motabang aron dili kita madakin-as, sama sa kapot sa sapatos sa salog!

copy.en: Friction is a force that resists motion. It slows down anything rolling or sliding across a surface!
copy.tl: Ang friction ay isang puwersang humahadlang sa galaw. Nagpapabagal ito sa anumang bagay na gumugulong o dumudulas!
copy.bis: Ang friction usa ka puwersa nga nagpugong sa lihok. Nagpahinay kini sa bisan unsang butang nga nagligid o nadakin-as!

assignedReviews.reason: The card compares static and sliding friction but does not address friction producing heat or ways to reduce/increase friction, which are the core actions of G5-F-3.

copy.en: It's harder to start a still object moving than to keep it going! The first push on a heavy cabinet is toughest — once sliding, it's easier. Friction is stronger on still objects!
copy.tl: Mas mahirap simulan ang paggalaw ng nakatigil na bagay kaysa padayunin! Ang unang tulak sa mabigat na aparador ang pinakamahirap — kapag gumalaw na, mas madali. Mas malakas ang friction sa nakatigil!
copy.bis: Mas lisod sugdan ang paglihok sa nakatigil nga butang kaysa padayonon! Ang unang tulod sa bug-at nga aparador pinakalisod — kung naglihok na, mas sayon. Mas kusog ang friction sa nakatigil!

copy.en: Car tires have grooves called treads to increase friction and grip the road, especially when wet! If treads wear down, the tire gets slippery and dangerous.
copy.tl: May mga ukit o treads ang gulong para dumami ang friction at kumapit sa kalsada, lalo na kapag basa! Kapag kapos na ang ukit, madulas na at delikado ito.
copy.bis: Ang ligid adunay mga ukit o treads aron modaghan ang friction ug mokapyot sa kalsada, ilabi na kung basa! Kung naupos na ang ukit, modanlog na ug delikado kini.

copy.en:
Ever wonder what happens when you stretch a spring?

When a spring is stretched or squeezed, it pushes or pulls back to its original shape!
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ba kung anong nangyayari kapag inuunat mo ang isang spring?

Kapag inuunat o pinipiga ang spring, gumaganti ito ng puwersa pabalik sa orihinal na hugis nito!
copy.bis:
Na-hanab-an ba nimo kung unsay mahitabo kon inaton nimo ang usa ka spring?

Kon inaton o pugson ang spring, mobalik kini og puwersa padulong sa orihinal niya nga porma!

copy.en:
Why is the Philippines a biodiversity hotspot?

Because it has thousands of endemic plants and animals — species found nowhere else on Earth!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na biodiversity hotspot ang Pilipinas?

Dahil libu-libong species ng halaman at hayop dito ay katutubo lamang sa bansa — walang matatagpuan kahit saan pa!
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag nga biodiversity hotspot ang Pilipinas?

Tungod kay libu-libo ka species sa tanom ug hayop dinhi ang endemic — wala gyud makita sa uban pang dapit!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light (an abiotic factor) and living things (fungi, animals) but does not describe or classify them as biotic and abiotic factors. It provides a specific ecological observation rather than teaching the concept of biotic/abiotic factors in an ecosystem.

copy.en: The forest floor gets very little sunlight because the tall canopy above blocks it — that's why mostly fungi and shade-loving animals live there.
copy.tl: Kaunti lang ang sikat ng araw na nakakarating sa sahig ng gubat dahil hinaharangan ito ng canopy sa itaas — kaya't fungi at mga hayop na kayang mabuhay sa dilim ang naninirahan dito.
copy.bis: Gamay ra ang kahayag sa adlaw nga moabot sa salog sa lasang kay giulohan kini sa canopy sa taas — mao nga fungi ug mga mananap nga kaya mabuhi sa ngitngit ang nagpuyo didto.

copy.en:
Is a fruit always sweet?

Not in science! A fruit is simply the part of a plant that holds the seeds, sweet or not. So some 'wild vegetables' with seeds inside are really fruits.
copy.tl:
Palaging matamis ba ang prutas?

Hindi sa siyensiya! Ang prutas ay ang bahagi ng halaman na may buto, matamis man o hindi. Kaya ang ibang 'ligaw na gulay' na may buto ay talagang prutas.
copy.bis:
Kanunay ba tam-is ang prutas?

Dili sa siyensiya! Ang prutas mao ang bahin sa tanom nga adunay liso, tam-is man o dili. Mao nga ang ubang 'ihalas nga utanon' nga adunay liso prutas gyud diay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's the part of the plant holding the seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: A wild fruit holding seeds is an outcome of seed production; the card does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the part of the plant holding the seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: A seed-holding fruit is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en:
What makes a fruit a "forest fruit"?

It grows wild on its own in the forest, not planted by people — and it's the part of the plant holding the seeds.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tinatawag na prutas sa gubat?

Bunga itong tumutubo mag-isa sa kagubatan, hindi itinanim ng tao — ito ang bahagi ng halaman na may buto sa loob.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gitawag nga bunga sa lasang?

Prutas kini nga motubo sa iyaha ra sa kagubatan, dili gitanom sa tawo — mao ni ang bahin sa tanom nga adunay liso sulod.
